newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish MPs foiled in bid to free wine sales.
newsitem.headline: Finnish MPs foiled in bid to free wine sales.

text.p: Finnish members of parliament campaigning to relax the grip of Alko, the retail monopoly on strong alcohol, have lost a bid to allow wine to be sold in ordinary shops, a government spokeswoman said on Thursday.

She said a petition signed by a majority of MPs, bidding either to relax the current law or at least to open up a debate on it, would not lead to any changes in the ruling which limits the sale of wine and spirits to Alko outlets.

Conservative Paula Kokkonen, who drew up the petition and collected 101 signatures in the 200-seat house, declined any immediate reaction but said she still believed it was only a matter of time before Finland relaxed the system.
"We thought the time would be right to allow Finnish people to make decisions themselves," she said of the petition.
Both Finland and neighbouring Sweden retain state retail monopolies on alcohol against European Union regulations, citing health and social reasons to win exemptions to EU rules.
Kokkonen said the Finnish government, which last year admitted it needed the revenue from high alcohol taxes to keep the budget intact, had contradictory reasoning.
"We are aware that a considerable portion of people in Finnish society has problems -- but the (alcohol) policy so far has not been very successful," she said.

Last month Swedes celebrated on the streets after an adviser at the European Court of Justice found largely in favour of a grocer who challenged its Systembolaget monopoly by selling wine over the counter in his shop.
The adviser said the retail monopoly system could not be justified on the grounds of protecting people's health.
